options.text:
( Mr. Bennet meets Colonel Forster and Mrs. Bennet in /gHertfordshire )
Mr. Bennet: So… Lydia ran off with Wickham, did she?
Colonel Forster: Yes, it appears so. I am truly sorry sir.
Mrs. Bennet: Lydia ran off?! 
Mrs. Bennet: My precious daughter!
Mr. Bennet: Don’t worry, I’ll go find her.
Mrs. Bennet: /sNo! Don’t go! /sWickham /swill /sruin /syou /stoo!
Mr. Bennet: (This woman…) I’ve got to do this or we will never get our daughter back…
Mrs. Bennet: /sNo! Please don’t do this! /sYou /sdon’t /shave /sto!
Mr. Bennet: (Why does she have to do this all the time?) I’m going if you like it or not!

And so the adventure begins!

(Mr. Bennet approaches an officer)
Mr. Bennet: Good day, sir.
Officer Adam: Good day to you too!
Mr. Bennet: Perchance, have you seen a young lady by the name of Lydia Bennet around here?
Officer Adam: I haven’t spoken to any lady since the day my mother passed…
Mr. Bennet: I’m sorry sir.
Officer Adam: However! I did see a young man running through this town with a lady, she looked ecstatic to be with him. I do wish I had some company though…
Mr. Bennet: Eureka! That sounds just like my Lydia! Which way were they headed?
Officer Adam: I believe they were headed that way, to… /gMeryton.
Mr. Bennet: I offer you my utmost gratitude for your service, good sir!
Officer Adam: Absolutely! (I sure do wish I had a daughter to save…)
( Mr. Bennet runs off to /gMeryton )

(Mr. Bennet approaches a woman wandering aimlessly about)
Mr. Bennet: Good day m’lady.
Beatrice (Looking away from Mr. Bennet): Are you trying to flirt with me sir! How disgusting!
Mr. Bennet: Absolutely not ma’am, I have a wife. I am not in need of your companionship!
Beatrice: Well then, I have a husband whom I am in an exceedingly happy marriage with!
Mr. Bennet: Anyway, have you seen a young lady-
Beatrice: What does your wife look like? Is she pretty?
Mr. Bennet: Not particularly but over the years we have come to understand each other.
Beatrice: Oh! Well, I’m not married, you can marry me, you know.
Mr. Bennet: (Sigh, god this woman is awful) I have already stated, I am not looking for your companionship! I am looking for a young lady, have you seen her?
Beatrice: Oh my! You’re with another lady?! What about your wife!
Mr. Bennet: She’s my daughter and she’s run off with a despicable sort of man. So, have you seen her?
Beatrice: Oh no, absolutely not! I’m blind after all!
Mr. Bennet: (What a horrible waste of time) Well goodbye then!
(Mr. Bennet, having learned absolutely nothing decides to make his way to /gHunsford to ask Mr. Collins about the situation)

(Mr. Bennet finds Mr. Collins)
Mr. Bennet: Well hello there Mr. Collins!
Mr. Collins: Why hello there to you too Mr. Bennet!
Mr. Bennet: Say, have you seen my lovely daughter Lydia run through here with Wickham as of recent.
Mr. Collins: I can’t say I have-
Mr. Bennet: (God what a waste of time) Thank you then Mr. Collins.
Mr. Collins: Wait! I did see them on their way to /gLondon when I was heading there myself last.
Mr. Bennet: Wha- Why thank you greatly, good sir!
Mr. Collins: Any time!
( Mr. Bennet hurries off to catch a carriage to /gLondon )

(Mr. Bennet approaches Mr. Darcy)
Mr. Bennet: Mr. Darcy!
Mr. Darcy: Why Mr. Bennet, what brings you to /gLondon on this fine cloudy day?
Mr. Bennet: Lydia ran off with Wickham and they are planning to leave the country! Have you any information on their whereabouts?
Mr. Darcy: Oh my! Indeed I do, I can bring you to them immediately.
Mr. Bennet: Thank you, sir!
Mr. Darcy: Although, I don’t believe we can keep Wickham in the country without some incentive…
Mr. Bennet: Well, if we force him to actually marry Lydia, there’s nothing he can do to get away, and he won’t be able to harm any more women!
Mr. Darcy: It’s settled then, we shall approach him, you will get your revenge and I will pay him off to get him to marry Lydia and get him to stay in the country.
